From detector signals to Δ(x,Q²): the reconstruction chain of the inclusive and coherent cos 2φ measurements

2026-08-24 · revised 2026-08-25 · companion to the cos 2φ projection report (money plots 5–7) and to plans/07 WP3 · computed with polligen.reco, polligen.hfs and polligen.recopseudo (evgen/scripts/: reco_chain_figures.py, hfs_resolution.py, money_cos2phi_reco.py, money_cos2phi_coherent_reco.py) · revision history in Appendix A

The projection report presents the double-helicity-flip structure function Δ(x,Q²) as φ′ pseudo-data and as extracted xΔ points. This note asks the experimentalist's question behind those plots: what does the detector actually record, event by event, in the inclusive and in the coherent intact-⁶Li measurement; how is the azimuth that carries the observable built from the reconstructed four-vectors and the known spin direction; which kinematic reconstruction assigns (x, Q²) to an event; which estimator turns spin-sorted φ′ histograms into an amplitude; and how the amplitude becomes Δ. It then states which of those operations the simulation performs (§5) and closes the chain at the reconstructed level (§7). Three of its results change the analysis design.

Three findings that change the analysis. (1) Three of the four inclusive sweet-spot bins of money plot 5 sit at y = 0.010–0.025, where the electron method gives δy/y = 50–120% even with a 1.2% calorimeter: x must come from the hadronic final state. At the documented 25% hadronic-y resolution the reconstructed sweet-spot bins keep 64–68% purity and their amplitude is within 1–9% of the true-bin value, known through the same response (§7). (2) The single-fill cos 2φ′ fit — the estimator of money plots 5–7 — measures the detector's own cos 2φ′ acceptance harmonic divided by Pzz: a 3% harmonic aligned with the vertical spin axis (the symmetry axis of both the crossing angle and the Roman-Pot cutout) fakes an amplitude four times the signal. The spin-state-sorted ratio of m = ±1-rich and m = 0-rich fills cancels any common acceptance bin by bin, turns relative-luminosity errors into a constant, and is 1.5× more precise. (3) In the coherent channel the anchored deformation term modulates the recoil azimuth φt − φS, not the electron azimuth used in the projection; the Roman-Pot cutout fakes ⟨cos 2φt⟩ ≈ 0.5 for a 25% aspect ratio (against a physics a₂ ≈ 0.036), and the near-beam cut is angular, so the tag acceptance is 67% / 9% / 10⁻⁸ at 20.5 / 50 / 137.5 GeV/u for the same optics.

1 · What is measured

Both measurements share the trigger object — a scattered electron in the central detector — and the spin bookkeeping of the ion beam. The coherent measurement adds the intact ⁶Li in the far-forward spectrometers and an exclusivity selection. The observable in both cases is not a cross section but a Fourier coefficient of a ratio of spin-sorted azimuthal distributions; Δ follows from that coefficient through kinematic factors and the unpolarized structure functions of the same data set.

2 · Angles and frames

For an unpolarized electron on a spin-1 target whose alignment axis has polar angle θS and azimuth φ relative to the virtual photon and the lepton plane, the Hoodbhoy–Jaffe–Manohar cross section for the projection state m reads [1,2]

and a fill with populations pm along a transverse axis (θS = 90°) has the φ′ distribution 1 + a₂ cos 2φ′ with

Which angle. The φ of the master formula is defined in a frame in which the target momentum P and the virtual photon q are collinear; it is the azimuth of the transverse spin about q measured from the lepton plane. The covariant definition used for every transverse-spin azimuth in SIDIS and exclusive analyses [3,4] applies verbatim to the spin four-vector S (and, with P′ in place of S, to the recoil azimuth of §4):

with g⊥ the projector orthogonal to P and q [3]. Evaluated in the head-on frame — ion along +z, electron along −z, the frame of the whole fast simulation — with a spin axis transverse to the beam at lab azimuth φS and the scattered electron at lab azimuth φe, this reduces exactly to φ′ = φe − φS for a massless target, and to the same with corrections of order γ² (below 5 mrad for γ² ≤ 0.02, i.e. everywhere in the sweet spots) for the massive nucleus (reco.azimuth_wrt_lepton_plane, verified against an explicit boost-and-rotate construction of the collinear frame to 10⁻¹³). The lab-angle shortcut is therefore legitimate for the inclusive measurement; the analysis evaluates the covariant formula anyway, because the coherent channel needs the same code.

Which frame. The beams cross at 25 mrad in the horizontal plane at IP6. The ePIC axis coincides with the electron beam, and the ion beam enters at −25 mrad in x (the convention of the far-forward gun scan in tools/fullsim). The head-on frame is reached by a rotation of 12.5 mrad about y followed by a boost βx = sin 12.5 mrad; energies change by 8×10⁻⁵ and the vertical spin direction is untouched. For the scattered electron the boost and the rotation cancel at first order because the detector axis is the electron axis: the residual distortion of its azimuth about the detector axis is an odd-harmonic effect of 0.7×10⁻³ (θ′ = 107 mrad) to 2.4×10⁻³ (383 mrad) in cos φ, with the cos 2φ harmonic untouched to 10⁻¹⁷ and the response of a true cos 2φ term equal to one within 10⁻⁵. The transformation is applied, but the crossing angle is not a source of a fake cos 2φ′ for the electron. It is one for the recoil (§4).

Orientation and the axis. The tensor alignment axis is headless — the m = +1 and m = −1 populations enter through cm = 3m² − 2 symmetrically — and cos 2φ′ is even under φ′ → −φ′ and φ′ → φ′ + π, so neither the orientation convention of φ nor the sign of n̂ can change the result. What matters is the axis direction modulo π: a misalignment δ of the assumed azimuth rotates the modulation, cos 2(φ′ − δ) = cos 2δ cos 2φ′ + sin 2δ sin 2φ′, so the fit should carry a sin 2φ′ term; since the only physics harmonic in the tensor ratio is cos 2φ′ (the m-symmetric fills set a₁ = 0, and the b₁-type constant is φ′-independent), the sin 2φ′ coefficient measures δ from the data themselves — a self-calibration of the spin axis at the precision of the modulation itself. A polar tilt ε of the axis out of the transverse plane dilutes by sin²θS = 1 − ε² (0.8% at 5°).

Harmonics from the tensor structure functions at finite γ. The exact spin-1 decomposition for unpolarized electrons (Cosyn et al. [12], Eq. 10) carries, besides the leading-twist Δ term, tensor-polarized pieces with the same azimuthal signatures: the combination of b₂, b₃, b₄ multiplying cos φTL is of order γ (their Eq. 17d), and the combination of b₂, b₃ multiplying cos 2φTT is of order γ² (Eq. 17e), with γ = 2Mx/Q. At the sweet spots γ² ≤ 0.023, so the b-type leakage into the cos 2φ′ amplitude is of order γ²(b₁/F₁)/6 ≈ 4×10⁻⁴ for b₁/F₁ ≈ 0.1 (a generous bound: HERMES' b₁ ≈ 0.11 at x = 0.012 corresponds to b₁/F₁ ≈ 0.01–0.02) — at most 3% of the Δ amplitude, at the high-x, low-Q² corner only, and computable from the same data's Azz; the O(γ) cos φ′ term is orthogonal to the cos 2φ′ fit at full coverage and becomes a by-product of the ratio fit. (For the axis along q the TLT and TTT parameters vanish, their Eq. 20 — which is why that axis is the clean choice for Azz and the transverse axis the only choice for Δ.) For x ≳ 0.2 at Q² ≈ 1 GeV² (γ² ≈ 0.1) the leakage grows to tens of percent of a 10⁻³ scenario, so the Azz-based subtraction is required there (docs/code_review_2026-08-25.md, item G2).

3 · The inclusive chain

  1. Event selection and electron identification. One e′ candidate with a track matched to an EMCal cluster; E/p and shower-shape cuts against π⁻ (photoproduction) and a charge-symmetric subtraction (wrong-sign tracks, positron running) for pair-symmetric background at high y. Efficiency εeID(η) = 0.70–0.95 in the ATHENA/ECCE anchors used by the money_delta study; no official ePIC curve exists.
  2. Scattered-electron kinematics. E′ from the calorimeter (2%/√E ⊕ 1%, i.e. 1.2% at E′ ≈ Ee) or the tracker (3% at η ≈ −3 in the tracking-only table), θ′ and φe from the track at the vertex (1–3 mrad), transformed to the head-on frame. The four-vectors k, k′, P and the spin four-vector S = (0, n̂) enter the covariant azimuth.
  3. Kinematic reconstruction. The electron method,

has a good Q² (δQ²/Q² ≈ δE′/E′ ⊕ cot(θ′/2)δθ′, dominated by the angle at the sweet spots: 5.2% for the 3 mrad track table used in §7 at θ′ ≈ 0.1 rad, 1.6% at spot 4, 2% if the backward disks reach 1 mrad — the track table is an unsourced placeholder) but loses y as (1 − y)/y: at y = 0.01 a 1.2% energy resolution gives δy/y = 120%, and the electron-ring energy spread alone (≈ 10⁻³) gives 10%. Table 1 shows where money plot 5 sits. At the mid-energy configuration three of the four sweet spots are at y = 0.010–0.025, the scattered electron carries 98–99% of the beam energy at η ≈ −2.9 to −2.4, and x is not measurable from e′ alone; at the top energy all four spots sit at y ≈ 0.01. The remedy is the one HERA used at low y [5,6]: y from the hadronic final state,

with θe measured from the ion direction. The Σ method is insensitive to collinear initial-state radiation, and both are insensitive to particles lost along the ion beam (E − pz ≈ 0 for forward remnants); their resolution is set by hadronic calorimetry and by losses in the electron direction. Three documented expectations bracket it: ATHENA uses e−Σ or DA for y ≲ 0.1 and quotes δy/y ≈ 25% at y ≈ 0.01, ≈ 10% at y ≈ 0.1, and 20–30% for JB throughout (its Sec. 3.1, Fig. 22) [18]; the ePIC kinematic-fit study smears the hadronic E − pz sum with σ(δh)/δh = 25% and finds Δy/y widths of 0.2–0.3 in 0.01 < y < 0.05, where the electron method is flat [19]; the ATHENA fast simulation of Arratia et al. gives RMS(y)/y ≈ 0.13–0.17 for IΣ, DA and JB at y ≈ 0.05–0.2 [20]. The band assumed here is 15–30%, with 25% central (the value used in §7). The low-energy configuration moves the same (x, Q²) to y = 0.05–0.25 (Table 1), so the energy scan is itself part of the reconstruction strategy for the x ≈ 0.1 bins.

Table 1 — the four sweet-spot super-bins of money plot 5 (selected per Q² band from the significance map at e(10)×⁶Li(50)) and where the same (x, Q²) bins sit at the low energy (y = Q²/(sx) with s = 4·5·20.5 GeV²); the top-energy spots are chosen by the same rule from the top-energy significance map and land at different x; Figure 1(b) places the re-selected spots of all three energies.

The hadronic final state in the chain. The hadronic y comes from a generated final state: polligen.hfs carries the hadronic final state of unpolarized DIS events through a hadron-side detector response and the Σ, Jacquet–Blondel and double-angle methods, and hands the result to the pseudo-experiments as a library — for a pseudo-event at (x, Q²) the captured fraction of Σ = Σ(E − pz) and the pT ratio of a generator event from the same (x, Q²) cell are applied to the pseudo-event's exact truth, the calorimeter noise is added per event, and y follows from the chosen method with the reconstructed electron. The tensor polarization enters only the inclusive azimuthal weight, so an unpolarized generator is the right source: the production sample is PYTHIA 8 (tools/pythia8/gen_dis_hfs.py, e + p and e + n at the per-nucleon beam energies, lepton radiation off), which runs in the eic-shell container; locally the chain runs on a toy string-fragmentation stand-in (hfs.ToyHFS), whose numbers are illustrative. The hadron-side response is the detection efficiency the measurement will live with: tracks within |η| ≤ 3.5 above pT = 0.2 GeV (95% plateau), calorimeter objects within |η| ≤ 3.7 (EMCal photons above 0.1 GeV; neutral and untracked charged hadrons in the HCal above 0.5 GeV at 90%), Yellow Report resolution requirements per region, and a Gaussian noise term on Σ and on each pT component (50 MeV by default, the magnitude Arratia et al. needed to reproduce the H1 full simulation at low y [20]). Figure 3 quantifies the toy: the detector captures 0.90 of Σ (0.60 in tracks, 0.30 in photons, 0.03 in neutral hadrons, the rest below threshold or beyond |η| = 3.7); without noise the Σ method resolves y to 9–12% everywhere in 0.005 < y < 0.1, and with 50 MeV of noise the resolution at the four sweet spots is 0.28 / 0.17 / 0.24 / 0.07 (Σ and JB alike; DA 0.37 / 0.29 / 0.28 / 0.10; the electron method 1.2 / 0.46 / 1.1 / 0.23) — the 25% used for §7 is what a 50 MeV noise floor does to a 0.2 GeV E − pz sum, and 100 MeV would double it. The noise and threshold floor of the ePIC calorimeters at Σh ≈ 0.2–0.5 GeV is therefore the number that decides the y ≈ 0.01 bins, not the relative resolution at high Σh; the PYTHIA sample replaces the toy's fragmentation, the response parameters stay the same, and both are run by evgen/scripts/hfs_resolution.py.

  1. The azimuth. φ′ = φe − φS from the covariant formula (§2), with φS the alignment-axis azimuth of that bunch from the spin bookkeeping. The track direction resolution enters the azimuth as σφ = σθ/sin θ′ ≈ 20–30 mrad at the sweet spots and dilutes cos 2φ′ by ⟨cos 2δφ′⟩ = 0.985–0.999 (§7): negligible.
  2. Binning in reconstructed (x, Q²). Figure 1(c) quantifies the migration for the mixed method with the sampler's own events: with δyhad/y = 15% (20%, 30%) the 3×3 super-bins keep a purity of 0.81–0.83 (0.74–0.77, 0.61–0.65) and the amplitude seen in the reconstructed bin is 0.98–0.99 (0.96–0.99, 0.92–0.98) of the true-bin value, because A(x) varies slowly across the bin. With the electron method alone the low-y spots collapse to purities of 0.41–0.56 with 26–53% of the events surviving in the bin. The correction is the standard migration matrix of any structure-function measurement; what is new is only that it must be built on the hadronic-method resolution.
  3. Spin-state sorting and the estimator. The events of each (x, Q²) bin are histogrammed in φ′ separately for each spin state f of the bunch pattern, Nf(φ′). Any smooth φ′-dependent efficiency ε(φ′) multiplies every Nf identically, so the bin-wise ratio

is free of ε(φ′) exactly (raw counts with luminosity-weighted wf, so that ΣfLfwf = 0), and a relative-luminosity error δf enters it only through P̄, as a φ′-independent constant plus a second-order rescaling (δ × P̄/σP²). The cancellation presumes that both spin states see the same ε(φ′): a difference of its cos 2φ′ harmonic between the m = ±1-rich and the m = 0-rich samples enters Â directly as (ε₂⁺ − ε₂⁰)/(P₊ − P₀) — 10⁻³ fakes half the signal — so the two states must alternate bunch by bunch within a fill (the pattern of Schematic 2), or the harmonic must be stable to 10⁻⁴ between fills (docs/code_review_2026-08-25.md, §5.1). A weighted least-squares fit of T(φ′) = c + d cos 2φ′ (+ e sin 2φ′), with T obtained from R bin by bin (the inversion is exact), gives Â = d after the finite-bin dilution sin w/w is divided out, and κ = c is the transverse tensor asymmetry of the b₁ sector, a by-product — whose sign follows the program's b₁ transcription rather than the HJM/HERMES convention (Cosyn et al. [12], Eq. 27: Azz = −(2/3)b₁/F₁; code review G1), which changes nothing in the Δ sector. For two fill types with equal luminosity the statistical error is

so that m = ±1-rich bunches at P+ = +0.6 alternated with m = 0-rich bunches at P0 = −1.2 (the same source purity gives −2P+, the pattern of the Azz run plan) are 1.5× more precise than a single Pzz = 0.6 fill with the whole luminosity; an unpolarized reference fill (P0 = 0) would instead cost a factor two. Figure 1(d) shows the pseudo-experiments: under an efficiency ε = 1 + 0.03 cos 2φ′ + 0.02 cos φ′ the single-fill fit returns Â = 0.062 for a true 0.0118 — the acceptance harmonic divided by Pzz — while the ratio is unbiased with the analytic error. A percent-level cos 2φ harmonic aligned with the vertical axis is to be expected (the crossing-angle plane is horizontal, module boundaries and dead areas are not azimuthally random, and the Roman-Pot cutout is a rectangle), so the spin-state-sorted ratio is the estimator of the measurement.

  1. Amplitude to Δ. With F₂ and R = σL/σT of ⁶Li per nucleon measured in the same data (the unpolarized cross section of the same sample, with its own radiative corrections) or taken from nuclear-PDF fits,

At the sweet spots the conversion is therefore insensitive to y — the (1 − y)/y² factor that makes low y attractive for the amplitude cancels against Dφ — and Δ/F₁ is essentially a direct ratio measurement; the y mis-measurement of the electron method affects the x label of the point, not the amplitude. Remaining corrections: the tensor rate shift (2/3)am(b₁ + …) in Dφ, at the 10⁻³ level and measured by κ; target-mass terms of order γ²; radiative corrections, uncalculated for tensor observables (plans/07 WP4); the per-nucleon and dilution conventions, which are interpretation rather than reconstruction; and the polarimetry scale δPzz/Pzz ≈ 3%, common with Azz.

4 · The coherent chain

The coherent measurement keeps steps 1–7 for the electron and adds the recoil. Its kinematics is fixed by two facts of the projection report: the recoil keeps the beam rigidity (R = 1.000 for A/Z = 2, and the momentum loss xP < 0.01 is below the Roman-Pot momentum resolution), so the only measured recoil quantity is its transverse displacement from the beam orbit; and coherence confines the sample to x ≲ 0.01, i.e. to y ≳ 0.05 at the mid energy (median x = 3.5×10⁻³, y ≈ 0.2), where the electron method is adequate and the low-y problem of §3 does not arise.

  1. Roman-Pot track. Hits in the two stations (AC-LGAD, ≈ 30 ps timing for bunch association) form a local track; the optics transfer matrices referenced to the beam orbit convert it to the angle pair (θx, θy) at the IP relative to the ion axis, so the crossing angle and the reference orbit are removed by construction, and the vertex from the central detector supplies the position term. The momentum fraction xL is set to 1 (unresolved), hence pT = A pu √(θx² + θy²) and φt = atan2(θy, θx). The resolution is dominated by the angular divergence of the bunch itself, δpT = A puσθ = 22 MeV at 50 GeV/u for σθ = 73 μrad, giving σ(φt) = 0.09 rad at pT = 0.25 GeV and a cos 2φt dilution of 1.5% (Figure 2d). The ePIC far-forward simulation with all beam effects (angular divergence, crossing angle, crab rotation and vertex smearing) gives ΔpT/pT ≈ 0.09 at 0.45 GeV and 0.04 at 1 GeV for 275 GeV protons, i.e. ΔpT ≈ 40 MeV, with the detector alone contributing ≤ 1.5% — "beam effects the dominant source of momentum smearing" [17]; ZEUS's leading-proton spectrometer was limited the same way (σ(t)/t = 0.14 GeV/√|t|, Φ resolution 0.2 rad) [13].
  2. Momentum transfer. Exactly, with xL = 1 − xP the plus-momentum fraction,

so the Roman Pots give t, and xP (or β = xA/xP) must come from the diffractive mass MX of the central detector (the HERA MX method [16]) — a coarse variable (a few xP bins), sufficient for the xP-dependence test of the two-component fit. The covariant recoil azimuth differs from the lab difference φe − φt by less than 0.2 mrad at these kinematics, so here too the lab shortcut is safe.

  1. Exclusivity selection. A beam-rigidity Roman-Pot track above the envelope; no OMD track (p at R = 0.5, ³He at 0.75 in the main window [8]), no ZDC neutron, no B0 EMCal photon (the 3.56 MeV state's de-excitation γ boosted to 0.1–0.4 GeV); a rapidity gap between X and the beam; Z-identification of the track if the pots resolve Z = 3 from 2 and 1 (open question #19), otherwise a two-component fit of the |t| spectrum against the ten-times-flatter α + d breakup slope; timing and vertex association against beam-gas coincidences. Because the incoherent cross section is m-state-blind, residual breakup dilutes the tensor ratio without faking it; its fraction is measured in the same data from the |t| fit.
  2. Three azimuths, two harmonics. With the recoil measured there are two physical azimuths besides the spin: α = φe − φS (lepton plane to axis) and β = φt − φS (recoil to axis), and α − β = φe − φt is the lepton-plane–recoil angle of unpolarized diffractive DIS. The rank-2 tensor polarization enters only through e±2iφS, so at leading power in the momentum transfer the spin-sorted distribution has the structure

The deformation term of the polarized-deuteron anchor — the modulation of the diffractive slope by the aligned gluon density, a₂(t) ∝ |t|, digitized in coherent.MANTYSAARI_A2_DEUTERON — is at: it lives in the recoil azimuth β, requires no photon helicity flip, and vanishes as t → 0 (the anchor defines Φ as the angle between the vector-meson momentum and the polarization axis in the γ*d c.m. frame and notes that at Q² > 0 the transformation from the lab "would mix the polarization states" [9] — the O(γ) mixing that the covariant definitions of §2 absorb). The double-helicity-flip term — the coherent counterpart of Δ, an interference of the two transverse photon helicities that needs the linear polarization of the photon and hence the lepton plane — is ae: it lives in α and is flat in t at leading power. The two mechanisms of the projection report are thus separated not only by their t-dependence but by the azimuth they modulate, which is a stronger discriminant; the mixed term am and the unpolarized u1,2 are nuisance harmonics. The latter are the L–T and T–T′ interference terms of diffractive DIS with a detected recoil, whose y-dependence is u₁ = (2−y)√(1−y) ALT/[2(1−y)+y²] and u₂ = 2(1−y) ATT/[2(1−y)+y²] [14]; ZEUS measured them with the leading-proton spectrometer as ALT = −0.036 ± 0.036, ATT = −0.030 ± 0.037 for xP < 0.01 and +0.051 ± 0.024, −0.010 ± 0.024 for 0.01 < xP < 0.1 — consistent with zero [13] — and the pQCD LT-interference model gives ALT ≈ 0.03 at our β ≈ 0.5, pT/Q ≈ 0.2 [15]; the pseudo-experiments of §7 use u₁ = 0.05, u₂ = 0.02, at the edge of the ZEUS bounds. The money-plot-6 pseudo-data place the anchored ⟨a₂⟩ on an axis labelled φ′ = φ − φS of the electron, which is the α axis: numerically harmless for a statistical projection, but the measurement must histogram (α, β) in two dimensions per (xP, t, Q²) bin and extract at and ae from the spin-state ratio R(α, β); in that ratio u(α − β) survives in the denominator, so the fit must carry it. An error δu in the assumed value does not stay second order: it reaches the pure harmonics as at·δu₂·⟨cos 2β⟩ and ae·δu₁, and with the cutout's fake ⟨cos 2β⟩ = +0.77 and at/ae ≈ 12–34 the first of these dominates — a ZEUS-1σ δu₂ = 0.024 shifts ae by 20%, 1.6 one-year statistical errors, while the same δu₁ moves ae by under 1% and shows up in the mixed term instead (§7.1). u₂, not u₁, is the nuisance to measure in situ from the spin-averaged counts of the same data.

The forbidden harmonics. With unpolarized electrons and a headless alignment axis the cross section is even under (α, β) → (−α, −β), so sin 2α, sin 2β and sin(α+β) are exactly zero: they are the coherent channel's null test, the counterpart of the inclusive sin 2φ′ term. Their pattern says which azimuth is misaligned — a spin-axis azimuth error δ rotates both tensor harmonics and gives sin/cos = tan 2δ in α and in β, whereas a Roman-Pot azimuthal roll δt leaves the lepton-plane harmonic exactly null and gives tan 2δt in β alone (verified to 10⁻⁵ in tests/test_recopseudo.py). Because at is an order of magnitude larger than ae, the recoil null is the sensitive one: it resolves a pot roll to 5–8 mrad per |t| bin in one year, while the α null resolves the spin axis only to 60–300 mrad — the inclusive sin 2φ′ fit does that job far better. The sin columns are orthogonal to the cos ones on the full grid, so the null costs nothing (§7). The t-dependent sine must use the same t-shape template as its cosine partner; with a plain ⟨sin 2β⟩ the null misses its own closure by 5%.

  1. Acceptance geometry and the estimator. The Roman-Pot acceptance is not a circular pT cut. The ePIC pots are 25.6 × 12.8 cm AC-LGAD planes surrounding a horizontal slot through which the beam, its momentum spread and its dispersion pass [17]: the cutout is wide in x and tight in y (the 10σ vertical beam size), a rectangle with cx ≫ cy whose sides are again horizontal and vertical — parallel and perpendicular to the spin axis. Anisotropy is the norm, not the exception: HERA's proton beam had a transverse-momentum spread at the interaction point of 45 MeV horizontally and 100 MeV vertically [13]. For the exponential recoil spectrum the tagged sample's azimuthal distribution is ε(φt) = exp[−B ρ(φt)²] with ρ the cutout boundary, and its ⟨cos 2φt⟩ (about the horizontal) is 0 for a square, +0.49 for an aspect ratio cy/cx = 1.25, +0.71 for 1.5, and −0.36 to −0.45 for the slot-like ratios 0.3–0.6 of Figure 2b (−0.77 for the wider slot of §7, 0.55 × 0.22 GeV) — ten to twenty times the anchored at ≈ 0.036, with the same symmetry axis (the sign flips when the axis is referred to the vertical spin direction). A square still carries ⟨cos 4φt⟩ = 0.34, which mixes into cos 2β at second order through the physics term. No single-fill fit can survive this; the spin-state ratio of §3 cancels it exactly, bin by bin in (α, β), and the same m = ±1-rich / m = 0-rich pattern serves both measurements.
  2. The near-beam cut is angular. The documented 0.20 GeV (high-acceptance) and ≈ 0.41–0.45 GeV (high-divergence) cuts are ten beam divergences times the 275 GeV proton momentum [7], σθ ≈ 73 and 149 μrad. The same envelope applied to a ⁶Li nucleus of momentum 6pu is pTcut = 10σθ·6pu: 0.09, 0.22 and 0.60 GeV at 20.5, 50 and 137.5 GeV/u, giving tag acceptances of 67%, 9% and 1.5×10⁻⁸ for B = 50 GeV⁻² (Figure 2c). The projection's constant 0.20 GeV cut (13.5%) is close to the mid-energy value and far from the others; whether the lithium divergence at a given energy equals the proton's is precisely the undocumented optics question of plans/04 #11, but the scaling with A pu is kinematics, not optics, and it makes the low-energy configuration the natural home of the coherent program (the alternative being the IR-8 secondary focus, which reaches pT ≈ 0 [10]).
  3. Resolution and unfolding. The divergence smearing moves the effective slope from B to 1/(1/B + 2δpT²) (47.7 for the numbers above) and smears |t| by 2pTδpT ≈ 0.01 GeV² — small against the 0.04–0.2 GeV² window (Figure 2d); the t-binning migration and the acceptance edge are unfolded with the same emulation, and tmin is a known bias of 3×10⁻³ GeV² at xP = 0.01 once xP is known from MX.

5 · What the simulation does

The table walks the chain of §§3–4 and states, for each step, what an experiment does and what the repository [11] does today. The generator kernel and the spin bookkeeping were complete from the start; the measurement layer — four-vectors, frames, kinematic reconstruction, the hadronic final state, the reconstructed azimuth, the spin-state ratio, the Roman-Pot measurement — is polligen/reco.py and polligen/hfs.py, composed by polligen/recopseudo.py into the pseudo-experiments of §7. The column worth reading is the last one.

Verdict. The chain is closed end to end at the reconstructed level, and three of its steps changed the headline numbers rather than their decoration: the hadronic-method requirement at the y ≈ 0.01 sweet spots (which changes the binning and the energy strategy, not the reach), the estimator (0.67× the error and one uncontrolled systematic removed), and the coherent angular cut together with the cutout geometry. What is still absent is everything downstream of the response — radiative corrections, an event-level breakup background, xP from MX, and an unfolding in place of the model bin-centering factor.

6 · What remains

The six recommendations of the first version of this note are carried out (§7 and Appendix A) except in three respects, which are the open items of the measurement design.

  1. The hadronic-resolution band. 5R and 7R are quoted at the 25% central value; the 15–30% band and the low-energy configuration for the x ≈ 0.1 bins are not yet run. The one number the analysis cannot produce for itself is the calorimeter noise and threshold floor at Σh ≈ 0.2–0.5 GeV, which is what decides the y ≈ 0.01 bins (plans/04 #21); the chain that turns it into a δy/y exists (§3).
  2. The coherent optics. The scan exists (evgen/scripts/coherent_optics_scan.py): at the slot cutout and B = 50 GeV⁻² the tagged fraction is 32% / 3.0% / 4×10⁻⁵ / 2×10⁻⁷ for a near-beam envelope of 0.10 / 0.22 / 0.45 / 0.60 GeV, and the one-year error on the deformation coefficient is 1.6% / 5.7% / 104% / 540% of it — so the coherent measurement lives at the low- and mid-energy configurations and is dead at the top energy, which is the quantitative form of the statement the letter needs. What remains is the cutout geometry itself, still an explicit assumption (plans/04 #20), and the IR-8 alternative, whose ⁶Li efficiency is our interpolation of the published d / ³He / ⁴He / ⁷Li values.
  3. Everything downstream of the response. Radiative corrections (WP4); an event-level α + d breakup background with the two-component |t| fit (plans/06); xP from the diffractive mass; an unfolding in place of the model bin-centering factor; and a fill-dependent φ′ efficiency, the one systematic the ratio estimator cannot cancel (§7.1).

7 · Reconstructed-level closure: money plots 5R, 7R and 6R

The chain of §§3–4 is composed in polligen/recopseudo.py. The inclusive response is importance-sampled: every accepted sampler cell (60×45 grid, generator cuts loosened to y ≥ 0.004, Q² ≥ 0.7 GeV², |η| ≤ 3.8, E′ ≥ 0.3 GeV so that events can migrate into the analysis window) receives 400 pseudo-events with weight σc/nkept (nkept = those inside the generator acceptance, so the cell rate is conserved), each carried through the lab frame (25 mrad crossing), Gaussian smearing of E′ (EMCal 2%/√E ⊕ 1%) and of the track direction (1–5 mrad by η), the head-on transformation, the electron-method Q², a hadronic y with the documented 25% resolution [18,19], the mixed-method x, the analysis cuts on reconstructed quantities, εeID(η), and the covariant φ′ on true and smeared four-vectors. The expected φ′ counts of any reconstructed bin are then exact bin integrals of denf + PfA cos 2φ′ summed over the events that land in it (the reconstructed-level analogue of phi_histogram_pseudo), Poisson- fluctuated at the 1-year and 10-year luminosities for the two fills of the m = ±1-rich / m = 0-rich pattern (bookkeeping.tensor_flip_plan), with the spin-axis-aligned efficiency ε(φ′) = 1 + 0.03 cos 2φ′ + 0.02 cos φ′ and a 10⁻³ relative-luminosity offset switched on. The estimator is the spin-state ratio fit of §3 with the sin 2φ′ term; Δ follows from the amplitude with the MC bin-centering factor K = Δmodel(xc, Q²c)/Amodel, reco bin, which includes the migration.

Efficiency = fraction of the true-bin rate reconstructed in the bin after εeID; D = ratio of the rate- and εeID-weighted, φ′-diluted model amplitude of the events in the reconstructed bin to the rate-weighted amplitude of the true bin. The last column is the single-fill, truth-binned error of the projection report.

Three observations. (i) The fit is unbiased at the reconstructed level: every Â agrees with its reco-bin truth within the statistical error while the acceptance harmonic and the luminosity offset are on, and the sin 2φ′ coefficients are consistent with zero. (ii) The two edge bins (spots 1 and 3 at y ≈ 0.01) lose about 60% of their events to the reconstructed y ≥ 0.01 cut and their amplitude reference shifts by 9% (the accepted half of the bin sits at lower true x); the analysis knows both through K, and the moment-constrained model's x-dependence is still resolved bin by bin (money plot 7R, best bins δΔ = 1.0×10⁻³ at Q² = 1.14 and 0.5×10⁻³ at 3.13 GeV² in year 1, purities ≈ 0.55). (iii) The errors are smaller than the truth-binned single-fill projection — 0.64–0.70 of the money-plot-5 values — because the 1.5× gain of the m = 0-rich fill outweighs the reconstruction efficiency of 0.37–0.64; this is the number to carry into plans/07 §7.1, with the caveat that it presumes the source delivers m = 0-rich bunches at |Pzz| = 1.2 (the same purity as the ±1 fill at 0.6).

Cross-check with the hadronic final state. Rerunning 5R with the hadronic y from the toy final state through the hadron-side response (Σ method, 50 MeV noise; money_cos2phi_reco.py --y-source hfs) instead of the 25% Gaussian gives purities 0.60 / 0.68 / 0.68 / 0.86, efficiencies 0.41 / 0.65 / 0.39 / 0.84, D = 0.900 / 0.939 / 0.913 / 0.986 and δÂ = 1.2 / 1.0 / 1.8 / 3.0 × 10⁻⁴ at the four spots — the same errors as Table 2, a worse spot 1 and a better spot 4 (where y = 0.05 and the resolution is 7% rather than 25%), with the fit unbiased and the median captured Σ fraction 0.99 for the selected events; 7R is unchanged (δΔ = 1.0×10⁻³ at Q² = 1.14 and 0.5×10⁻³ at 3.13 GeV² in year 1). The Table 2 numbers therefore stand as long as the calorimeter noise floor is ≈ 50 MeV; they degrade in proportion to it.

Coherent channel (money plot 6R). The coherent response samples recoils from the exponential spectrum with xP ∈ [10⁻³, 10⁻²], builds the exact four-vector, and emulates the pots with the angular envelope 10σθ·6pu at σθ = 73 μrad (0.22 GeV at 50 GeV/u), a slot-like cutout |px| < 0.55, |py| < 0.22 GeV (the horizontal slot of the ePIC sensor planes [17], its width illustrative), and divergence smearing. The two-azimuth expected counts per fill are exact α-integrals per event of 1 + u₁cos(α−β) + u₂cos 2(α−β) + Pf[aecos 2α + at(t) cos 2β + amcos(α+β)] with the true β and t inside and the reconstructed β and |t| = pT² for the binning. Two lessons follow. First, the anchor convention: the full text of the deuteron paper fixes d²σ/dΦd|t| ∝ 1 + 2ΣnaneinΦ (its Eq. 9, with Φ the angle between the vector-meson momentum and the polarization axis in the γ*d frame), so the cos 2β coefficient is 2a₂ — the deformation modulation is twice what money plot 6 injects (c₂ = −(Pzz/2)εB0B|t| = 0.072 at ⟨|t|⟩ = 0.06 GeV² and Pzz = 0.6; coherent.cos2phi_coefficient_deformation). Second, the cutout makes the in-bin β distribution far from uniform (the acceptance varies by more than an order of magnitude around the circle) and correlates β with |t| inside a reco t bin (the blind directions hold the larger-|t| recoils), so the harmonic fit must use the acceptance-weighted basis from the response — ⟨cos 2β⟩, ⟨cos β⟩, ⟨sin β⟩ per bin, and for the t-dependent term the template ⟨(t/tref) cos 2β⟩ of the assumed linear shape — which is exactly the two-component fit a₂(t) = cdef|t| + ag of plans/06 in MC-response form. With the analytic (uniform-bin) basis the deformation coefficient is biased by 3–6% in the lowest t bin (1.25-aspect cutout); with the template it closes. A third, geometric lesson: the slot concentrates the tagged recoils near β ≈ 0 and π, where cos 2β hardly varies, so the lever arm on the deformation harmonic shrinks — its statistical error is three times that of a square cutout of similar acceptance (0.007 against 0.002 in the first |t| bin at one year), while the electron-azimuth term ae is untouched. The pot geometry is therefore a design lever for the deformation measurement and irrelevant for the exotic-glue one.

7.1 · Audit notes and known limits

Checked independently of the code that produced the numbers: the analytic error of the two-fill ratio, 2√(2/N)/(P+−P0)/dilution, reproduces the pseudo-experiment spreads and the printed errors (spot 1: 1.21×10⁻⁴ for N = 1.72×10⁸); the exact expected counts reproduce the sampler's generator-level effective_modulation when binned in truth (test); the bin-centering factor returns the injected Δ exactly without noise (test); the sign of the deformation term is positive for Pzz > 0 and εB0 < 0, consistent with the predicted sign flip relative to the deuteron; the Eq. (9) convention was read from the paper's text, not inferred; the relative-luminosity immunity is second order (δ·P̄/σP² — a 2% offset moves the amplitude by 0.7%, a 10⁻⁴ offset by 3×10⁻⁵); empty φ bins inside the cutout are handled with zero weight; the α-integrals of the coherent counts are analytic per event and the β smearing is absorbed in the MC basis, so the fitted coefficients refer to the unsmeared truth.

Known limits, stated rather than hidden. The hadronic y of Table 2 is a parametrized 25% Gaussian — an absolute 50–125 MeV on Σh = 0.2–0.5 GeV at the sweet spots — reproduced by the toy final state with a 50 MeV noise floor (§3), so the open item is the noise and threshold floor of the real detector at that Σh and the PYTHIA fragmentation in place of the toy (plans/04 #21); u₁, u₂ are generated at the ZEUS 1σ bounds [13] and the slot dimensions are illustrative (#20); the φ′-efficiency harmonics are illustrative magnitudes; radiative corrections and backgrounds are not included; the 7R points are centered with the injected model (as in money plot 7); the template assumes the linear t-shape it fits, so a different shape is a model systematic to be varied.

Detector nuisances, measured. Each is switched on in the response and the amplitude converted with the nominal K, so the quoted number is the shift of Δ̂ it produces (money_cos2phi_reco.py --syst-scan, common random numbers; the MC noise floor of the response is 0.13–0.21% at the four spots). A 1% electron energy-scale error moves Δ̂ by 0.2–1.4% — the larger of the two energy levers, since d ln x/d ln E′ = 2 − y for the Σ method against −(1 − y) for the hadronic scale (the Gaussian y stand-in never sees E′ and gives only 1, so it understates this systematic by about two). Generating at a 30% hadronic resolution and correcting with the 25% response shifts Δ̂ by 0.5–1.3%. An η slope of 0.05 per unit on εeID gives 0.02% — the estimator is a weighted mean of per-event amplitudes, so a smooth efficiency shape is almost exactly null, and a flat one is exactly null. Replacing the backward-endcap calorimeter specification by the Yellow Report table per η region changes nothing at spots 1–3 (their electrons are backward) and 0.5% at spot 4, whose η = −1.64 reaches the transition region. All four sit below the 3–11% model dependence of K.

From the code review (docs/code_review_2026-08-25.md): the φ′ efficiency of Table 2 is common to both fills, and the ratio cancels only a common acceptance. The fill-dependent case is now modelled rather than argued — a difference δε₂ of the cos 2φ′ efficiency harmonic between the m = ±1-rich and m = 0-rich samples enters Â as δε₂/(P₊ − P₀), verified against the pseudo-experiments (reco.fill_acceptance_bias): δε₂ = 10⁻³ fakes 5.6×10⁻⁴, which is 5% of the sweet-spot amplitudes but 4.6 times the one-year statistical error and 14 times the ten-year one. Bunch-by-bunch alternation, or stability of the harmonic to ≈ 10⁻⁴ between fills, is therefore a requirement of the measurement. The coherent counterpart is tighter than the earlier estimate: a naive δ⟨cos 2β⟩/(P₊ − P₀) gives 1.3% of at for a 1% change of the vertical envelope between fills, but the fit gives +19% for a 10⁻³ change and +169% for 1% — under the slot only half the β bins are live and the t-shape template is 99% anti-correlated with the constant there, so a shape perturbation is amplified about a hundredfold. The requirement is bunch-by-bunch alternation or ≈ 10⁻⁴ envelope stability; the mitigation, if neither is available, is that the higher-|t| bins are far less exposed (+3.9% and +0.04% at the same 10⁻³ for |t| = 0.08–0.12 and 0.12–0.17 GeV², where more of the circle is live). K is model-dependent at the 3–11% level between the repository's Δ shapes (moment_A/moment_B/toy at the four spots), larger than the 10-year statistical errors; the EMCal term 2%/√E ⊕ 1% is the backward specification applied at all η (the sweet-spot electrons are backward, the high-x bins of the amplitude panels are not); the 6R sample is background-free and Z-identified by assumption. u₁, u₂ and the luminosity shares are exactly known in Table 3, but no longer only by assumption: they are arguments of the fit (measure_coherent(u_coeffs_assumed=, lumi_assumed=, responses=), money_cos2phi_coherent_reco.py --u2-assumed --rel-lumi-offset --envelope-split), and the sensitivities above are what they produce. The relative luminosity is second order here as it is inclusively (10⁻³ moves at by 0.08%).

2026-08-25Editorial pass: the note restated as current content. The audit table and §6 give today's status rather than the history of the code; the implementation recipe of the old §5.1 is dropped in favour of §7; the duplication between the lede, the verdict and the recommendations is removed.
Conventions: head-on frame with the ion along +z and the electron along −z; θ′ is the scattered-electron angle from the electron beam; per-nucleon (x, y, s) throughout; whole-nucleus four-momenta where a mass matters. Beam divergences are the proton values implied by the documented Roman-Pot cuts (73 and 149 μrad); the lithium optics are undocumented (plans/04 #11). Built by reports/build_report.py; figures from the evgen/scripts named in the text; display mathematics typeset at build time.
